title: Trent Alexander-Arnold dropped for Real Madrid derby fixture due to lateness
content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold has been dropped for Real Madrid’s starting line-up against Atletico Madrid for being late to training this week.

This marks the second league game in a row that he has not been a part of. Alexander-Arnold was left on the bench against Elche, as head coach Alvaro Arbeloa wanted to give him some rest, but returned to the starting line-up for Madrid’s win against Manchester City on Tuesday.

Sources with knowledge of the situation, left anonymous to protect relationships, confirmed that the England international’s absence on Sunday was a form of punishment after he didn’t arrive on time to a training session.

The same sanction was applied to Marcus Rashford in September, as Hansi Flick dropped him from Barcelona’s starting line-up to face Getafe for being late to training that day.

Alexander-Arnold, 27, has made 20 appearances in his first season at Madrid after moving from Liverpool in the summer, despite missing multiple weeks with a hamstring injury and then sustaining a right thigh issue.

The right-back was left out of Thomas Tuchel’s 35-man England squad this week for this month’s friendlies against Uruguay and Japan, the final two games before the head coach names his provisional World Cup squad. Tuchel called the choice a “sporting decision” to stick instead with Jarell Quansah (who has since dropped out), Tino Livramento and Djed Spence.

Madrid entered their fixture against Atletico second in La Liga, seven points below Barcelona though the Catalan club have played one more game.
